pr_comments: Thank you! I gave this a spin with the ~7.5k of corrupted journals I currently have at hand and nothing crashed; sanitizers were happy as well.

> Thank you! I gave this a spin with the ~7.5k of corrupted journals I currently have at hand and nothing crashed; sanitizers were happy as well.

Just out of curiosity (and maybe for any readers): would your test know if these changes just prevented the operation from doing the work?  I assume yes, but it'd be nice to see confirmation that this can't possibly be 7.5k of corrupted journals NOOP'd into success now.
@vcaputo this test makes sure that stuff doesn't crash. It can't confirm that the code works correctly.

> > Thank you! I gave this a spin with the ~7.5k of corrupted journals I currently have at hand and nothing crashed; sanitizers were happy as well.
> 
> Just out of curiosity (and maybe for any readers): would your test know if these changes just prevented the operation from doing the work? I assume yes, but it'd be nice to see confirmation that this can't possibly be 7.5k of corrupted journals NOOP'd into success now.

Yeah, as Evgeny said, it just makes sure `journalctl` doesn't die with a signal, it doesn't check if the action taken makes "sense", since there's just way too many error paths. But for that we have the integration test suite, which should do these checks instead (to some degree).

@mrc0mmand on a somewhat related note I think it would be great to run `journalctl` under Valgrind with that corpus. It should help to somewhat replace MSan (which would be used on OSS-Fuzz if that AFL++ PR got merged). That would be slow though so it would make sense only if it could be incorporated in a daily/weekly cron job.

> @mrc0mmand on a somewhat related note I think it would be great to run `journalctl` under Valgrind with that corpus. It should help to somewhat replace MSan (which would be used on OSS-Fuzz if that AFL++ PR got merged).

That sounds like a good idea, especially given your recent findings :)

> That would be slow though so it would make sense only if it could be incorporated in a daily/weekly cron job.

Depends. Running it only once against the directory full of journals (e.g. `journalctl --directory=...)` should be fairly quick and could be incorporated directly into TEST-04-JOURNAL. However, running it for every journal would indeed be quite slow (it's slow even without valgrind).
